library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2022_caspofungin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wu_2022_caspofungin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.02249-21>
* Open-access full text: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9116478/>

Wu 2022 studied caspofungin in critically ill adults in a surgical ICU after
cardiac surgery. Twenty-seven had received a heart transplant and 31 had had
other cardiac surgery. Heart transplantation did not affect caspofungin PK once
serum albumin was accounted for: the final two-compartment model keeps only
albumin, as a power covariate on clearance. Lower albumin gives a higher
clearance, which the authors attribute to a larger unbound fraction of this
highly protein-bound drug.

# Population

Fifty-eight patients at one centre in Guangzhou, China (July 2019 - July 2021),
gave 414 plasma samples (Results and Table 1). The heart-transplant group had a
median age of 50 years, weight 59.5 kg, 19% women and a median albumin of
40.3 g/L (29.7-49.3). The control group had a median age of 58 years, weight
62.0 kg, 32% women and a median albumin of 33.7 g/L (26.41-48.40). About half
of each group was on CRRT and about a quarter on ECMO; the median SOFA score was
9-10. Every patient received a 70 mg loading dose and then 50 mg every 24 h as a
1-h intravenous infusion. Samples were taken before the dose and 1, 2, 6, 10,
16 and 24 h after it, on at least 3 days.

# Source trace

The supplementary material prints the NONMEM control stream. Its `$THETA` and
`$OMEGA` values agree with Table 2, and it supplies the albumin centring value
(37.42 g/L) that the main text does not print.

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment model, IV infusion (ADVAN3 TRANS4) | -- | Results; supplementary control stream `$SUBROUTINES` |
| `lcl` (CL at ALB = 37.42 g/L) | 0.385 L/h | Table 2; control stream THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (Vc) | 4.27 L | Table 2; THETA(2) |
| `lq` (Q) | 2.85 L/h | Table 2; THETA(3) |
| `lvp` (Vp) | 6.01 L | Table 2; THETA(4) |
| `e_alb_cl` | -1.01 | Table 2, 'theta ALB-CL'; THETA(7) |
| `etalcl` | 0.112 (33.5%) | Table 2; control stream `$OMEGA` |
| `etalvc` | 0.455 (67.5%) | Table 2; `$OMEGA` |
| `etalq` | 0 FIX | Table 2; `$OMEGA` |
| `etalvp` | 0.2275 (47.7%) | Table 2 (`$OMEGA` prints 0.22) |
| `propSd` | 0.134 | Table 2; THETA(5) |
| `addSd` | 0.213 mg/L | Table 2; THETA(6) |
| CL = THETA(1) exp(ETA(1)) (ALB/37.42)^THETA(7) | -- | Control stream `$PK`; Methods equation 2 |
| W = IPRED THETA(5) + THETA(6), `$SIGMA 1 FIX` | -- | Control stream `$ERROR` |
| 70 mg loading, then 50 mg q24h, 1-h infusion | -- | Methods, 'Blood sample collection' |
| PTA: AUC = Dose / CL; AUC/MIC targets 865, 450, 1185 | -- | Methods, 'Simulations'; supplementary Matlab code |

# Virtual cohort

Each group has 100 subjects. Albumin is drawn log-normally around each group's
Table 1 median, with a log-scale SD of one quarter of the log range, and is
truncated to the observed range. Albumin is held constant within a subject.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2022)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)
n_arm <- 100

draw_alb <- function(n, med, lo, hi) {
  sdl <- log(hi / lo) / 4
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(med), sdl))
    out <- c(out, x[x >= lo & x <= hi])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

subj <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_arm), group = "Heart transplant", ALB = draw_alb(n_arm, 40.3, 29.7, 49.3)),
  data.frame(id = n_arm + seq_len(n_arm), group = "Control", ALB = draw_alb(n_arm, 33.7, 26.41, 48.40))
)
subj |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_ALB = median(ALB), min_ALB = min(ALB), max_ALB = max(ALB), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "Median ALB (g/L)" = median_ALB, "Min" = min_ALB, "Max" = max_ALB) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort albumin.")
```

```{r events}
inf_dur <- 1
dose_times <- seq(0, 96, by = 24)
dose_amts <- c(70, rep(50, length(dose_times) - 1))
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 120, by = 0.5), dose_times + 1)))

make_events <- function(s) {
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = s$id, time = dose_times, evid = 1, amt = dose_amts,
    rate = dose_amts / inf_dur, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = s$id, time = obs_times, evid = 0, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  ev <- rbind(dose, obs)
  ev$ALB <- s$ALB
  ev$group <- s$group
  ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}
events <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(subj, subj$id), make_events))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Wu_2022_caspofungin")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("group"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Concentration-time profiles

The paper's VPC (Figure 3) overlays observed data, which are not available.
The plot below shows the simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles over the
first five days for each group.

```{r profiles}
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Caspofungin (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Simulated 70 mg loading dose, then 50 mg q24h (1-h infusion)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 3 does not say which dosing day its Cmax, Cmin and AUC describe. The
third dose (48-72 h), the last of the minimum three sampling days, is used.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)
dose <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, group)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | group + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | group + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 48, end = 72, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))$result)

nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES), q05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    q95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(parameter = nlmixr2lib::ncaParamLabel(PPTESTCD)) |>
  dplyr::select(group, parameter, median, q05, q95) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "NCA parameter" = parameter, "Median" = median,
    "5th percentile" = q05, "95th percentile" = q95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated NCA of the third dose (Cmax, Cmin in mg/L; AUC in mg.h/L).")
```

## Comparison against the published values (Table 3)

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  group = c("Heart transplant", "Control"),
  cmax = c(11.74, 7.89),
  cmin = c(3.59, 2.92),
  auclast = c(126.86, 105.64)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  params = c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs published medians (Wu 2022 Table 3). * differs by >20%.")
attr(cmp, "footnote")

# Centre-of-distribution check (one value per simulated subject, so assert on
# the median only): AUC is set by CL and its albumin covariate.
auc_med <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published[, c("group", "auclast")], by = "group")
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_med$auc / auc_med$auclast - 1) < 0.12))
```

The AUC matches Table 3 in both groups. The higher albumin of the
heart-transplant group lowers its clearance in the model, which reproduces that
group's higher AUC. The simulated Cmin is 17-20% below Table 3 in both groups.
Cmax is the weak point: the heart-transplant Cmax matches, but the control
Cmax is about 38% too high. Table 3 reports individual Vc medians of 3.14 L in
the heart-transplant group and 5.27 L in the control group. The model has no
covariate on Vc, so both groups share the 4.27 L typical value, and the
simulated Cmax hardly differs between groups. Table 3 summarises individual
(post hoc) estimates, so this group difference sits inside the model's 67.5%
IIV on Vc rather than in its fixed effects.

## Replicate Figure 4 (probability of target attainment)

The paper computes PTA from the steady-state AUC over 24 h, AUC = Dose / CL,
with clearance log-normal across subjects (Methods, 'Simulations'). The values
below use the model's typical clearance at the 37 g/L albumin of Figure 4 and
its CL IIV. The AUC/MIC targets are 865 (*C. albicans*), 450 (*C. glabrata*)
and 1185 (*C. parapsilosis*).

First, the PKNCA steady-state AUC from a typical-value solve is checked against
Dose / CL, which the PTA calculation relies on.

```{r ss-auc}
typ_ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 50, rate = 50 / inf_dur, ii = 24, addl = 19, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 480, by = 0.1)) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_ev$ALB <- 37
typ_ev$id <- 1L
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), typ_ev, returnType = "data.frame")
typ$id <- 1L
cl_typ <- typ$cl[1]

ss_nca <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ[, c("id", "time", "Cc")], Cc ~ time | id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(typ_ev[typ_ev$evid == 1, c("id", "time", "amt")], amt ~ time | id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 456, end = 480, auclast = TRUE)
))$result)
auc_tau <- ss_nca$PPORRES[ss_nca$PPTESTCD == "auclast"]
c(cl_typical = cl_typ, auc_tau = auc_tau, dose_over_cl = 50 / cl_typ)
# Same drawn parameters on both sides (no IIV): pure numerical error.
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_typ - 0.385 * (37 / 37.42)^-1.01) < 1e-8,
  abs(auc_tau * cl_typ / 50 - 1) < 0.005
)
```

```{r fig4}
omega_cl <- sqrt(0.112)
targets <- c("C. albicans" = 865, "C. glabrata" = 450, "C. parapsilosis" = 1185)
pta_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  species = names(targets),
  dose = c(50, 70, 100, 150, 200),
  mic = c(0.03, 0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    target = targets[species],
    pta = pnorm((log(dose / (mic * target)) - log(cl_typ)) / omega_cl)
  )

ggplot(pta_grid, aes(mic, pta, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~species, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA", colour = "Dose (mg)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Wu 2022 (median lines; ALB = 37 g/L)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The maintainers read the median PTA lines of Figure 4 at points where the
lines are steep, so a parameter error would show:

```{r fig4-compare}
fig4 <- data.frame(
  species = c(rep("C. albicans", 5), rep("C. glabrata", 5), rep("C. parapsilosis", 5)),
  dose = c(50, 70, 100, 150, 200, 50, 70, 100, 150, 200, 50, 70, 100, 150, 200),
  mic = c(0.125, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.125, 0.125, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5),
  pta_fig4 = c(0.70, 0.29, 0.71, 0.37, 0.71, 0.67, 0.24, 0.66, 0.32, 0.67, 0.33, 0.74, 0.33, 0.80, 0.33)
)
fig4_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(fig4, pta_grid, by = c("species", "dose", "mic")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = pta - pta_fig4)
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(species, dose, mic, pta_fig4, pta, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Species" = species, "Dose (mg)" = dose, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic,
    "PTA, Figure 4 (read)" = pta_fig4, "PTA, model" = pta, "Difference" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Model PTA against values read from Figure 4.")

# Deterministic (no random draws). The tolerance covers reading the figure
# and the paper's use of bootstrap-median parameters in its Matlab code.
stopifnot(max(abs(fig4_cmp$diff)) < 0.06)
```

The model reproduces Figure 4 to within the precision of reading the figure.

## Albumin dependence (Figure S1)

Figure S1 repeats Figure 4 at other albumin levels. Because CL scales as
(ALB / 37.42)^-1.01, the AUC scales almost in proportion to albumin. The table
gives the 50 mg dose's PTA against *C. albicans*.

```{r albumin}
alb_tab <- tidyr::expand_grid(ALB = c(25, 30, 37, 45, 50), mic = c(0.06, 0.125, 0.25)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl = 0.385 * (ALB / 37.42)^-1.01,
    pta = pnorm((log(50 / (mic * 865)) - log(cl)) / omega_cl)
  )
alb_tab |>
  dplyr::select(ALB, mic, pta) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("ALB (g/L)" = ALB) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "PTA, 50 mg q24h, C. albicans (AUC/MIC > 865).")
```

## Structural checks

The albumin covariate equation is checked against hand calculation.

```{r covariate-check}
one <- function(alb) {
  e <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 1), evid = c(1, 0), amt = c(50, 0), cmt = "central", ALB = alb)
  r <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), e, returnType = "data.frame")
  r[1, c("cl", "vc", "q", "vp")]
}
m25 <- one(25)
m3742 <- one(37.42)
stopifnot(
  abs(m3742$cl - 0.385) < 1e-8, abs(m3742$vc - 4.27) < 1e-8,
  abs(m3742$q - 2.85) < 1e-8, abs(m3742$vp - 6.01) < 1e-8,
  abs(m25$cl - 0.385 * (25 / 37.42)^-1.01) < 1e-8
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Albumin centring.** The Methods describe continuous covariates as
  (cov / cov_ave)^theta without printing the average. The supplementary
  control stream and Matlab code both use 37.42 g/L, which is used here. The
  Methods call 37 g/L the median, and Figure 4 is drawn at 37 g/L.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV in percent. The control stream `$OMEGA`
  values (0.112, 0.455, 0.22) are the squares of the Table 2 percentages
  divided by 100, so the percentages are sqrt(omega^2). The Vp variance uses
  the more precise Table 2 value, 0.477^2 = 0.2275. The paper's Matlab code
  instead converts the bootstrap CL percentage as a CV, sqrt(log(CV^2 + 1));
  the difference is small (0.319 against 0.335) and Figure 4 is reproduced
  either way.
* **IIV on Q.** Fixed to zero in the final model (Table 2, `$OMEGA 0 FIX`),
  kept as `etalq ~ fixed(0)`.
* **Residual error.** The control stream sets the residual SD to
  IPRED x 0.134 + 0.213 (a linear sum, `$SIGMA 1 FIX`), encoded with
  `combined1()`.
* **Time-varying albumin.** Albumin was recorded on each sampling day. The
  virtual cohort holds it constant within a subject; the model accepts a
  time-varying column.
* **Table 3 comparison.** The paper does not say which dosing day Table 3
  describes. The third dose is used. Table 3's group difference in Cmax is not
  explained by the model's covariates, so the control-group Cmax is
  overpredicted (see the comparison above).
* **Figure 4.** The paper's Matlab code samples bootstrap uncertainty and plots
  the median PTA across 1000 draws. The replication uses the final estimates
  without parameter uncertainty, which gives the median lines but not the
  shaded intervals.
